SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: STORY TELLING
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES · Grade: Grade 3
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Story Telling helps you succeed in LITERACY ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: STORY TELLING
Study Story Telling like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.

What this means
In this part you learn to use digital knowledge to  Learners listen to stories from various digital SPEAKING create stories platforms and use the same platforms to create their. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use digital knowledge to  Learners listen to stories from various digital SPEAKING create stories platforms and use the same platforms to create their.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Story Telling”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use digital knowledge to  Learners listen to stories from various digital SPEAKING create stories platforms and use the same platforms to create their. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Story Telling is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Story Telling”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: use digital knowledge to  Learners listen to stories from various digital SPEAKING create stories platforms and use the same platforms to create their)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Story Telling to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: use digital knowledge to  Learners listen to stories from various digital SPEAKING create stories platforms and use the same platforms to create their.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Story Telling from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Story Telling: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 3 learner study Story Telling?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What do stories LISTENING the learner should be able to: techniques of story telling teach us?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Story Telling means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: use digital knowledge to  Learners listen to stories from various digital SPEAKING create stories platforms and use the same platforms to create their.
